reports.title: Minnesota field reports

scope.name: Minnesota DNR reporting offices
scope.description: Selected office observations from a statewide reporting page. The state outline locates the report, not surveyed coverage or flock positions.

reports.method: Narrative observations compiled from state and federal wildlife managers and surveys; these summaries are not standardized abundance estimates.
reports.headline: Different pictures across the state.
reports.summaryNote: DNR described arrivals in several regions, with stronger numbers in the south and west.

regions.name: Fergus Falls
regions.note: More birds, including mallards; lake levels remained low.

regions.name: Roseau River WMA
regions.note: Bird numbers and activity declined; pool habitat remained favorable.
regions.mallardObservation: Mallards appeared in harvest observations; no abundance count supplied.

regions.name: Lac qui Parle WMA
regions.note: No clear influx of new birds; wetlands were drying.

regions.name: Appleton
regions.note: Small, temporary arrivals without a major concentration.

reports.provenance: Official page Updated October 29, 2026; embedded weeklyWaterfowlReport records General, Fergus Falls, Roseau River WMA, Lac qui Parle WMA, Appleton, and Aitkin.
notes: These are dated field observations. Weather expectations stated in the original report belong to that report week, not today's forecast.
Hunter harvest descriptions are not converted into bird abundance.

reports.title: South Dakota field reports

scope.name: South Dakota reporting regions
scope.description: Six agency reporting regions. The state outline is a geographic reference; regional boundaries and flock positions are not inferred.

reports.method: Regional agency field narratives. Directional observations are retained without assigning counts or numerical migration bonuses.
reports.headline: Some arrivals; water still matters.
reports.summaryNote: Reports described uneven arrivals and dry wetlands in parts of the state.

regions.name: Northeast
regions.note: Migration remained slow; mallards were scarce and divers were gathering.

regions.name: East Central
regions.note: Some new mallards followed northern cold and light snow.

regions.name: Southeast
regions.note: Mixed duck arrivals used areas holding water.

regions.name: Lower River / South Central
regions.note: Several duck species arrived, but many waterholes remained dry.

regions.name: James River Valley
regions.note: Duck numbers improved after north winds, including mallards.

regions.name: Pierre / Central
regions.note: Birds increased around Mobridge; farther south, groups remained scattered.

reports.provenance: Official 2026 Waterfowl Report, Week of October 26, six regional sections before Week of October 19.
notes: Regional descriptions do not establish exact departure times, arrival times, or standardized counts.
